name: MS-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+14 district with an entrenched Republican incumbent seeking re-election
Guest holds roughly $962,000 cash on hand versus about $23,000 for Chiaradio
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 98%; no polls or expert ratings show competition
Libertarian on the ballot but not a competitive factor
model.rationale: Guest combines a fourteen-point Republican district lean with a lopsided financial advantage, and neither polling, expert ratings, nor outside spending signals any Democratic traction. Markets price his re-election near certain, justifying a forecast slightly more Republican than the raw fundamentals alone.
model.watch: A late scandal or a sudden influx of outside spending against Guest could narrow the race, though nothing currently points in that direction.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's 3rd District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Michael Guest is seeking re-election with the advantages that typically come with the seat. He has raised more than $820,000 and holds nearly $1 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Michael Chiaradio has raised about $155,000 with only $23,000 available. A Libertarian, Erik Kiehle, also appears on the ballot. No public polls survey the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets put Guest's chances at roughly 98%, consistent with the district's fourteen-point Republican lean and his incumbency. The absence of polling leaves some room for error, but nothing in the fundraising picture, the candidate profiles, or the broader environment suggests a serious Democratic threat. The seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands in November.
